sections.title: Design Specification
sections.content:
**Overview**
Resolves import/include statements from source files into project-internal file paths and builds symbol-to-definition-file maps used for cross-file usage tracking.

- Use `resolve_module_to_project_path` when you have a module name from an import statement and need to know which project file (if any) it refers to.
- Use `build_symbol_to_file_map` when analyzing a file's imports and need a dict mapping imported/referenced names to the file that defines them, plus alias resolution.
- Use `detect_source_roots` once per project to discover which source-root prefixes (e.g. Java/Kotlin/Scala layout) are actually present, so later resolution calls can retry with those prefixes.
- Use `get_import_params` to obtain the tree-sitter `Language` and import query string needed before parsing a file's imports for a given extension.

This file relies on `codetwine/config/settings.py` for language-specific behavior (`IMPORT_RESOLVE_CONFIG`, `SOURCE_ROOT_PATTERNS`, `SAME_PACKAGE_VISIBLE`, `DEFINITION_DICTS`, `IMPORT_QUERIES`, `TREE_SITTER_LANGUAGES`), on `codetwine/parsers/ts_parser.py`'s `parse_file` to parse files whose definitions must be registered, and on `codetwine/extractors/definitions.py` (`extract_definitions`, `DefinitionInfo`) to enumerate the names defined in a resolved file. It is used by `file_analyzer.py`, `pipeline.py`, `extractors/usage_analysis.py`, and `extractors/dependency_graph.py` to resolve imports into project files and to build the symbol maps that drive cross-file usage detection and dependency graph construction.

Path resolution and candidate generation are entirely config-driven (no per-language `if` branches for candidate generation), keeping language differences isolated to `IMPORT_RESOLVE_CONFIG`. Symbol registration deliberately overwrites on name collisions but logs a warning via `_put_symbol`, favoring last-import-wins semantics over raising errors.

**Definitions**

## `detect_source_roots`
Checks each pattern in `SOURCE_ROOT_PATTERNS` (e.g. `"src/main/java/"`) against a project's file path set and returns only the prefixes that actually appear as a prefix of at least one file. Used once per project (by `pipeline.py` and `dependency_graph.py`) to build the `source_root_set` passed into later resolution calls, avoiding blind prefixing attempts for layouts the project doesn't use.

## `resolve_relative_import`
Converts a raw module string from an import statement (e.g. `"..utils"`, `"./helper"`, `"os"`, `"com.example.Foo"`) into a list of path components relative to the project, handling Python dot-relative imports (counting leading dots to walk up `current_dir_part_list`) and JS/TS `./`/`../` relative imports (normalized via `os.path.normpath`) separately from plain absolute imports (split by separator). It is the first step used internally by `resolve_module_to_project_path` and has no other external caller.

## `generate_candidate_path_list`
Produces an ordered, deduplicated list of candidate file paths for a given `base_path`, driven declaratively by an `IMPORT_RESOLVE_CONFIG` entry's flags (`try_init`, `index_ext_list`, `alt_ext_list`, `try_bare_path`, `try_current_dir`). Handles Python `__init__.py` packages, JS/TS directory `index` files, alternate extensions, C/C++ bare-path includes (e.g. `stdio.h`), and current-directory-relative fallbacks; avoids appending a redundant extension when `base_path` already ends in a known extension from `alt_ext_list`.

## `resolve_module_to_project_path`
Resolves an import's module name to an actual project file path by combining `resolve_relative_import` and `generate_candidate_path_list`, then matching candidates against `project_file_set`, falling back to prefixing each entry in `source_root_set` (e.g. turning `com/example/Foo.java` into `src/main/java/com/example/Foo.java`) if no direct match is found. Returns `None` for standard-library or external-package modules that don't resolve to any project file; this is the core entry point used throughout the codebase (`usage_analysis.py`, `dependency_graph.py`, `build_symbol_to_file_map`) wherever an import needs to be tied to a project file.

## `_put_symbol`
Registers a name into `symbol_to_file_map`, logging a warning via `logger` when the name already maps to a different file, so overwrites during symbol-map construction are traceable rather than silent. Used internally by all symbol-registration paths in this file.

## `build_symbol_to_file_map`
Builds the `(symbol_to_file_map, alias_to_original)` pair used by usage tracking to determine which file a referenced name comes from, given a list of `ImportInfo` objects for a file. Applies language-specific rules read from `IMPORT_RESOLVE_CONFIG`'s `separator` field: Python registers module roots and `from X import a, b` names individually (with `*` triggering full-file definition registration via `_register_definitions_from_file`), Java/Kotlin register the trailing class name and skip package-root registration, and C/C++ `#include` registers all definitions from the included file. Also handles Java/Kotlin wildcard imports (`import com.foo.*`) by falling back to `_register_definitions_from_package`, and appends same-package-visible symbols (via `SAME_PACKAGE_VISIBLE`) from sibling files in the same directory sharing `file_ext`, so classes usable without explicit import are still resolvable.

## `_register_definitions_from_file`
Parses a single project-relative file with `parse_file` and registers every top-level definition name (via `extract_definitions` and `_select_top_level_definitions`) into `symbol_to_file_map`, skipping the file silently if it doesn't exist on disk or has no configured `DEFINITION_DICTS` entry for its extension. Used wherever an entire file's contents are considered "brought in" by an import (C/C++ `#include`, Python `from X import *`, Java/Kotlin same-package or wildcard-package visibility).

## `_select_top_level_definitions`
Filters a line-sorted `DefinitionInfo` list down to only the outermost (non-nested) definitions by tracking the end line of the last selected definition and skipping any definition that starts within that covered range. Exists to prevent class members (methods, fields, constructors) from being registered as standalone importable symbols mapped to an unrelated class's file.

## `_register_definitions_from_package`
Handles Java/Kotlin wildcard imports (`import com.example.model.*`) by locating all project files directly under the corresponding package directory—trying both the bare package path and each `source_root_set` prefix—and registering their definitions via `_register_definitions_from_file`, explicitly excluding files in sub-packages (paths containing an extra `/` after the prefix) so only direct package members are included.

## `get_import_params`
Looks up the tree-sitter `Language` object and import query string for a given file extension using `IMPORT_QUERIES` and `TREE_SITTER_LANGUAGES`, returning `(None, None)` when the extension is unsupported so callers can cleanly skip import analysis for that file. Used as the first step before parsing imports in `file_analyzer.py`, `usage_analysis.py`, and `dependency_graph.py`.

summary: Resolves import/include statements into project file paths and builds symbol-to-definition-file maps for cross-file usage tracking. Key functions: detect_source_roots, resolve_relative_import, generate_candidate_path_list, resolve_module_to_project_path, build_symbol_to_file_map, get_import_params, plus internal helpers (_put_symbol, _register_definitions_from_file/_package, _select_top_level_definitions). Config-driven per-language behavior (Python, Java/Kotlin, C/C++, JS/TS) via IMPORT_RESOLVE_CONFIG. Used by file_analyzer, pipeline, usage_analysis, dependency_graph for import resolution, alias handling, source roots, wildcard/package visibility.
